title: Sylva: terrestrial and airborne laser scanning processing for forest ecology
description:
Sylva is an open-source library and command-line tool for processing terrestrial, mobile and airborne laser scans of forests for ecology and remote-sensing research. A Rust core holds every computation and file format; Python gets a numpy-friendly API and a sylva command over it. It reads and writes LAS/LAZ, PLY, XYZ, RIEGL RXP and RDBX and RiSCAN PRO projects, and covers ground classification and terrain models, subsampling and filtering, marker-free coregistration of scan positions, tree segmentation, stem detection and diameter at breast height, cylinder quantitative structure models with volumes and branch orders, leaf and wood separation, ray-traced voxels with plant area density and occlusion, gap-fraction and plant area index profiles, scan quality assessment, change detection between survey epochs, airborne lidar over tiled areas with area-based and individual-tree metrics, fusion of terrestrial and airborne data, full-waveform decomposition, and synthetic scenes with known answers for testing.

Install with pip install sylva-rs; the Rust crate is on crates.io as sylva-rs. Documentation is at uq-eorc.github.io/Sylva.
